<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="436.9mm" height="88.5mm" viewBox="0 0 436.9 88.5" data-device="tm-8104" data-view="front" data-weight-kg="14.5" data-weight-note="9 to 14.5 kg by configuration (data sheet)" data-overall-mm="482 x 88.9 x 350 with rack ears (the data sheet's 133.35 height is a 3RU slip)" data-switching-capacity="1.2 Tbps full duplex, wire speed, non-blocking" data-port-options="40x SFP+; 40x SFP+ + 4x QSFP28; or 88x SFP+ (with the 48-port module)" data-power-max-w="400" data-power-envelope="unstated" data-power-envelope-note="data sheet "Max power consumption 400W", no configuration or ambient stated" data-input-voltage="AC, or DC 24 / -48 V" data-psu-redundancy="dual redundant, hot-swappable" data-cooling="load-sharing, speed-controlled, hot-swappable fans (TM810x-FAN)" data-operating-temp="0 to 50 C" data-humidity="up to 95 percent, non-condensing" data-expansion-slots="1" data-oam-module="TM810x-OAM, full-FPGA expansion module for hardware OAM (location not documented)" data-services="MPLS L2VPN (VPLS, H-VPLS, VPWS), MPLS L3VPN (BGP), 802.1Q, 802.1ad Q-in-Q" data-routing-protocols="IS-IS, OSPF, BGP, RSVP-TE, LDP, Segment Routing, xSTP, G.8032, LACP, MC-LAG" data-resiliency="sub-50 ms RSVP-TE FRR, secondary LSP, G.8031 1:1, G.8032, dual-homed VPLS/H-VPLS, BFD" data-oam="hardware IEEE 802.1ag CFM, 802.3ah EFM, Y.1731 SLM/DMM, Y.1564 and RFC 2544 test head, MEF 46/48/49" data-timing="SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 PTP, BITS, 1PPS and ToD (DS-v14)" data-local="CLI console and out-of-band Ethernet on RJ45" data-mgmt-protocols="Console, Telnet, SSHv2, RADIUS, TACACS+, SNMP v1/2/3, xFTP, NTP, DNS resolver, NETCONF" data-emc="EMC Directive 2014/30/EU including EN 300386; FCC 47 CFR Part 15 Class A; ICES-003:2020 Issue 7 Class A" data-safety="LVD Directive 2014/35/EU; UL 62368-1 / CAN CSA-C22.2 No. 62368-1; Class 1 laser product IEC 60825-1" data-rohs="RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU, Directive (EU) 2015/863" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="436.9mm" height="88.5mm" viewBox="0 0 436.9 88.5" data-device="tm-8104" data-view="front" data-weight-kg="14.5" data-weight-note="9 to 14.5 kg by configuration (data sheet)" data-overall-mm="482 x 88.9 x 350 with rack ears (the data sheet's 133.35 height is a 3RU slip)" data-switching-capacity="1.2 Tbps full duplex, wire speed, non-blocking" data-port-options="40x SFP+; 40x SFP+ + 4x QSFP28; or 88x SFP+ (with the 48-port module)" data-power-max-w="400" data-power-envelope="unstated" data-power-envelope-note="data sheet "Max power consumption 400W", no configuration or ambient stated" data-input-voltage="AC, or DC 24 / -48 V" data-psu-redundancy="dual redundant, hot-swappable" data-cooling="load-sharing, speed-controlled, hot-swappable fans (TM810x-FAN)" data-operating-temp="0 to 50 C" data-humidity="up to 95 percent, non-condensing" data-expansion-slots="1" data-oam-module="TM810x-OAM, full-FPGA expansion module for hardware OAM (location not documented)" data-services="MPLS L2VPN (VPLS, H-VPLS, VPWS), MPLS L3VPN (BGP), 802.1Q, 802.1ad Q-in-Q" data-routing-protocols="IS-IS, OSPF, BGP, RSVP-TE, LDP, Segment Routing, xSTP, G.8032, LACP, MC-LAG" data-resiliency="sub-50 ms RSVP-TE FRR, secondary LSP, G.8031 1:1, G.8032, dual-homed VPLS/H-VPLS, BFD" data-oam="hardware IEEE 802.1ag CFM, 802.3ah EFM, Y.1731 SLM/DMM, Y.1564 and RFC 2544 test head, MEF 46/48/49" data-timing="SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 PTP, BITS, 1PPS and ToD (DS-v14)" data-local="CLI console and out-of-band Ethernet on RJ45" data-mgmt-protocols="Console, Telnet, SSHv2, RADIUS, TACACS+, SNMP v1/2/3, xFTP, NTP, DNS resolver, NETCONF" data-emc="EMC Directive 2014/30/EU including EN 300386; FCC 47 CFR Part 15 Class A; ICES-003:2020 Issue 7 Class A" data-safety="LVD Directive 2014/35/EU; UL 62368-1 / CAN CSA-C22.2 No. 62368-1; Class 1 laser product IEC 60825-1" data-rohs="RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU, Directive (EU) 2015/863" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="436.9mm" height="350mm" viewBox="0 0 436.9 350" data-device="tm-8104" data-view="bottom" data-weight-kg="14.5" data-weight-note="9 to 14.5 kg by configuration (data sheet)" data-overall-mm="482 x 88.9 x 350 with rack ears (the data sheet's 133.35 height is a 3RU slip)" data-switching-capacity="1.2 Tbps full duplex, wire speed, non-blocking" data-port-options="40x SFP+; 40x SFP+ + 4x QSFP28; or 88x SFP+ (with the 48-port module)" data-power-max-w="400" data-power-envelope="unstated" data-power-envelope-note="data sheet "Max power consumption 400W", no configuration or ambient stated" data-input-voltage="AC, or DC 24 / -48 V" data-psu-redundancy="dual redundant, hot-swappable" data-cooling="load-sharing, speed-controlled, hot-swappable fans (TM810x-FAN)" data-operating-temp="0 to 50 C" data-humidity="up to 95 percent, non-condensing" data-expansion-slots="1" data-oam-module="TM810x-OAM, full-FPGA expansion module for hardware OAM (location not documented)" data-services="MPLS L2VPN (VPLS, H-VPLS, VPWS), MPLS L3VPN (BGP), 802.1Q, 802.1ad Q-in-Q" data-routing-protocols="IS-IS, OSPF, BGP, RSVP-TE, LDP, Segment Routing, xSTP, G.8032, LACP, MC-LAG" data-resiliency="sub-50 ms RSVP-TE FRR, secondary LSP, G.8031 1:1, G.8032, dual-homed VPLS/H-VPLS, BFD" data-oam="hardware IEEE 802.1ag CFM, 802.3ah EFM, Y.1731 SLM/DMM, Y.1564 and RFC 2544 test head, MEF 46/48/49" data-timing="SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 PTP, BITS, 1PPS and ToD (DS-v14)" data-local="CLI console and out-of-band Ethernet on RJ45" data-mgmt-protocols="Console, Telnet, SSHv2, RADIUS, TACACS+, SNMP v1/2/3, xFTP, NTP, DNS resolver, NETCONF" data-emc="EMC Directive 2014/30/EU including EN 300386; FCC 47 CFR Part 15 Class A; ICES-003:2020 Issue 7 Class A" data-safety="LVD Directive 2014/35/EU; UL 62368-1 / CAN CSA-C22.2 No. 62368-1; Class 1 laser product IEC 60825-1" data-rohs="RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU, Directive (EU) 2015/863" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>
